correctness.rationale: For the explicitly normalized F16 Fourier-zero code, the rank of 5+2 characters gives dimension 282. A Vandermonde argument excludes support below four. Rectangles force nonzero new exponents; Lagrange interpolation constructs legal F16 four-words from vanishing four-subset divided differences. Exact GF256 arithmetic exhausts all 2380 four-subsets for every exponent 0..16, yielding 16 necessary (u,v) pairs in two symmetry orbits. Two explicitly stated and directly replay-verified nonzero four-position words obstruct the representatives (3,6) and (6,8); sign inversion and coordinate swap cover the rest. These checks, not random samples, are carried out in the embedded verifier and paired with an analytic completeness proof. No conclusion beyond the fixed one-orbit family is claimed.

value.rationale: The originating paper poses the natural task of adding one Fourier cyclotomic orbit to raise the basic abelian code distance to five and demonstrates success for q=8. Resolving the next power-of-two field q=16 in the opposite direction, for every possible added orbit, identifies a genuine construction boundary. The finite exact vanishing profile and explicit symmetry-class witnesses give a motivated complete classification beyond substituting a number into a published formula; the result is useful for deciding when this canonical extension method cannot produce a better code.
